verdict.rationale: Docusaurus's `npm run build` command generates static files into a `build` directory, and the deployment docs say they can be served from any static host (Vercel, GitHub Pages, Netlify, Render, Surge). The MIT license and source content kept as MDX/Markdown further support the no-lock-in goal. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of hosting the built bundle on arbitrary infrastructure (community posts discuss build times, not portability).

support.subject: As a developer, I can export my entire docs site as a static bundle and host it anywhere, so my content is never locked in

citations.quote: To build the static files of your website for production, run: npm run build
Once it finishes, the static files will be generated within the `build` directory.

You can deploy your site to static site hosting services such as [Vercel](https://vercel.com/), [GitHub Pages](https://pages.github.com/), [Netlify](https://www.netlify.com/), [Render](https://render.com/docs/static-sites), and [Surge](https://surge.sh/help/getting-started-with-surge).
Docusaurus builds them into static HTML files ready to be served.
